chapter: New York with Lester Young and Coleman Hawkins
title: Boogie-woogie from Pete Johnson and Albert Ammons; his love for Lester Young
summary: In New York Johnson and Ammons taught him boogie-woogie; he loved Lester Young, wanted to play tenor, and modelled his piano style on Lester.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: But I finally went on to New York, and it was there that I was inspired by other great piano players like Pete

Johnson and Albert Ammons became very influential in my life, and they taught me the boogie-woogie style. And Pete Johnson was a very warm human being. And he and Albert Ammons both. And the fact of the matter is the way I went to New York was I was sent to play with Lester Young, who was my real love. Actually Lester Young was my real love, because I like to play tenor too.
Yes, I always liked to play tenor.

Well it was hard on the teeth, and of course then I'd already established myself as a piano player, and it wasn't really the time to devote to it. And then you know, you can't learn everything at once, but I always loved Lester Young, and really I tried to pattern my playing after Lester Young on the piano, and that's what really established my original style of playing until, as I said, met Art Tatum who taught me more about the piano itself, you know.
